title: The Program — a trainee track for Options, visually
lede: The series, run the way a trading firm runs a trainee class: a short track of ideas in order, a pit where you answer against a clock, and a ledger that decides what you practice next. The pages show you a thing happening. This page finds out whether you can do it.

chapters.title: Where option edge comes from, and what kills each kind
chapters.dek: A map of where to look. It is not evidence that the edge is there today.
chapters.text: Every trade worth doing sits in one of these families. Before putting one on, name the family, the signal and its number, the structure that isolates it, who is on the other side, and what kills it. If one of those is blank, the trade is not ready. 1 · Carry and financing Mispriced The interest rate, dividend or borrow implied by call minus put. Signal The rate a conversion, box or jelly roll locks in, against your own funding. Structure Conversion, reversal, box, jelly roll. Other side Someone paying for financing or for a hard-to-borrow short through the options. What kills it A dividend change, early assignment, a pin, a borrow recall. A low implied rate is usually the borrow fee, not cheap money. The edge is cents, so costs decide it. Drill Chain Box 2 · Exercise and corporate actions Mispriced Mostly your own leakage: value given away by a wrong exercise, tender or adjustment call. Signal Exercise a call the night before the ex-date only if the dividend beats the interest on the strike plus the put you throw away. Structure The exercise decision itself, and cleaning up near-the-money positions before expiry. Other side Nobody pays you. You stop paying others — and holders who fail to exercise hand the dividend to whoever is short. What kills it Assignment is random, so hedge to the expectation and size for the spread. Pin risk dwarfs the intrinsic at stake. The exercise chain itself can fail. Drill Early exercise Dividend play Pin risk Read Early exercise · Mergers 3 · Vol level Mispriced The whole level of implied vol against what the stock will realize. Signal A clean base vol plus events, compared with the market. A month of realized vol is a noisy estimate. Structure Straddle or variance, delta-hedged. Other side Short: buyers of insurance. Long: overwriters and put sellers pressing vol down. What kills it Path dependence — the moves land where your gamma is. Hedging error. Jumps. P&L that arrives in lumps. Drill Clean vol Fair vol and edge 4 · Term structure and events Mispriced One expiry out of line with its neighbors, or an event move priced wrong. Signal Forward vol between expiries; the event move backed out of two expiries. Structure A calendar, sized by root-time vega; front against back across the event. Other side Hedgers and lottery buyers in the front expiry. What kills it A calendar that is flat in raw vega is short the front. Short-dated vol moves more. Fat tails. Drill Event move Term structure 5 · Skew and curvature Mispriced One tail against the other, or the wings against the middle. Signal The risk reversal and the fly against their own history. Structure Risk reversal, delta-hedged; fly, or strangle against straddle. Other side Buyers of crash insurance; overwriters on the call side. What kills it Your delta depends on how you assume the smile moves. A regime change makes history a trap. Read The surface 6 · Correlation Mispriced Index vol against the vols of its components. Signal Implied correlation. Above one means a bad mark. Structure Short index variance, long single-name variance. Other side Index hedgers. What kills it Correlation goes to one in a crash while single-name vols rise. It often loses on the first leg down. Drill Implied correlation 7 · Flow and relative value Mispriced A name cheap or rich to its peers and its own history because of who is trading it. Signal Where its vol sits in its own cone, and who the flow is. Structure Buy the cheap vol, sell the rich, hedge the direction. Other side The flow itself: overwriting programs, structured products, put sellers. What kills it Cheap that is only a flow artifact. Crowding. A premium that lasted years and then reversed. Drill Peer group Read The playbook · Vol cone 8 · Providing liquidity Mispriced Nothing. You are paid the spread for standing there. Signal Where the price goes after your fills. Structure Quote the edge in vol points, hedge the delta, manage the rest by leaning your vols. Other side Anyone who needs to trade now. What kills it Adverse selection: the fills you get are the ones you would rather not have. Read Microstructure 9 · Broken bounds Mispriced A butterfly priced below zero, or total variance that falls with expiry. Signal The sign of the cost, checked before any Greek. Structure Sell the body and buy the wings; sell the near expiry and buy the far. Other side Usually nobody: a stale or wide quote. What kills it It does not trade where it is marked. Check the quote is live before believing it. Drill Call prices Mock pit
